Subject: MAP: Hosting comparison & perf eval plan (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Elena / Carlos — attaching the first draft of the mutual action plan and the performance evaluation checklist. The goal is to validate latency, throughput, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency behavior across our three hosting modes so you can pick the right trade-offs before close.

High-level MAP milestones (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): confirm test dataset, security checklist, and desired SLOs.
- Week 1: Redwood runs baseline perf sweep (cold & warm, 1–64 concurrent sessions).
- Week 2: Joint validation with your load generator in your region; run isolation tests and autoscale perturbations.
- Week 3: Final report + recommended config + signoff and commercial close.

Evaluation plan notes (what we'll measure):
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 for token streaming across typical prompt lengths (64/256/1024 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec and sequences/sec at different batch sizes.
- TTFT: cold-start (empty KV cache + model cold) and warm-start (hot KV cache).
- Concurrency: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 sessions; measure inter-request variance and per-session fairness.
- Autoscaling behavior: time-to-scale-up, scaling overshoot, and recovery path under sudden load spikes.
- Isolation: run noisy-neighbor synthetic test to observe p95 tail amplification on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Deliverables attached: acme_map_v1.pdf (MAP milestones & responsibilities), bench-results-hosted-dedicated-private.csv (raw results), chart-ttft-concurrency.png (visual summary).

Please review and confirm: 1) the SLO numbers you care about (we put examples in the MAP), 2) test data and any redaction rules, and 3) who from your infra/security should be on the Week 2 validation call.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Elena — thanks for the questions. Quick answers up front: TTFT is measured at the gateway (request arrival) to first byte streamed to the client. For private tests we can either run from your VPC peered test subnet or emulate from our private staging; your preferred approach is peered VPC for fidelity. Autoscale events in Dedicated/Private use pre-warmed pools when configured; cold node joins can add ~80–220ms to TTFT depending on model size and quantization. More detail below and a short summary table from our Week 1 sweep is attached (bench-results-hosted-dedicated-private.csv).

Summary of key numbers (selected rows, prompt length ~256 tokens, mixed batch sizes):
- Hosted (multi-tenant): p50 latency streaming = 140ms, p95 = 720ms, throughput = 18k tokens/sec (aggregate across batchers), TTFT cold = 420ms, TTFT warm = 170ms, high variance during noisy-neighbor spike (+220ms p95).
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): p50 = 130ms, p95 = 340ms, throughput = 26k tokens/sec, TTFT cold = 310ms, TTFT warm = 150ms, much tighter tail and predictable autoscale when pre-warm set > 2 nodes.
- Private (customer VPC/on-prem): p50 = 120ms, p95 = 280ms, throughput = 24k tokens/sec, TTFT cold = 650ms (first cold node boot), TTFT warm = 140ms; isolation best-in-class once instance pool is warm, but initial cold-start when cluster scales from zero can be slow (model load + KVS restore).

Autoscaling behavior observations:
- Hosted: aggressive horizontal burst capacity but p95 spikes when external external traffic saturates shared batchers; recommend request-level retry and client-side token backpressure for production SLOs.
- Dedicated: predictable scale with <60s scale-up to target when pre-warm=1; recommend pre-warm=2 for 99.9% TTFT SLO at expected peaks.
- Private: recommend keeping at least one warm node for primary region; cold cluster boot (when scaled from 0) can be 40–120s depending on infra and model size — consider scheduled warm windows where traffic is predictable.

Recommendations for the MAP (updates):
- Update target SLOs to the numbers above and call out buffer capacity (pre-warm nodes) per hosting mode.
- Include autoscale test step in Week 2 where Acme triggers a sudden 5x traffic spike for 3 minutes and we measure recovery and error rates.
- For sensitive dataset: use our redaction-in-transit flow (we'll provide an upload token for a short-lived staging bucket).

Next steps: 1) confirm you want peered VPC for Week 2 validation, 2) confirm redaction flow contact (ops/security person), 3) agree to updated MAP milestone: shift final signoff to Jun 10th to allow for a one-week remediation window if we spot regressions.

Attaching: bench-results-hosted-dedicated-private.csv, chart-ttft-concurrency.png

Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
